characterList.description: An older Asian man with short grey hair wearing a pink mitre, a green chasuble with gold trim over a white alb, and a white Roman collar.
characterList.name: Bishop

content_metadata.description: This video explores the concept of obedience to God and its three stages: offering (alay), pain (aray), and acceptance (Amen), as explained by the Bishop in a church setting.

qAndA.answer: The painting depicts Jesus ascending to Heaven after His resurrection. It symbolizes hope, transcendence, and the ultimate victory over suffering and death, offering a visual counterpoint to the Bishop's discussion of pain and doubt.
qAndA.question: What is the significance of the painting shown in Scene 5 (3:20)?

qAndA.answer: The statue visually reinforces the Bishop's message about surrendering to God's will, even in the face of adversity. Mary, as the mother of Jesus, represents acceptance of God's plan, even when it involves sacrifice and pain. The baby Jesus symbolizes innocence and trust in God's love.
qAndA.question: What is the role of the statue of Mary and baby Jesus shown in Scene 6 (5:59)?

qAndA.answer: The Bishop encourages listeners to embrace the challenges of faith, emphasizing that true discipleship involves offering oneself to God wholeheartedly, even when faced with pain, doubt, and adversity. He suggests that through surrendering to God's will, even in death, one can find ultimate freedom and meaning in life.
qAndA.question: What is the main message conveyed by the Bishop in the video?

qAndA.answer: The Bishop's tone initially is engaging and introspective, inviting reflection on obedience. It becomes more somber as he discusses doubt and questioning God. However, his tone shifts to hopeful and encouraging as he emphasizes perseverance and God's unwavering presence. Finally, his tone becomes calm and reassuring, conveying acceptance and surrender to God's will.
qAndA.question: How does the Bishop's tone change throughout the video?

qAndA.answer: The cuts create a sense of communal experience and highlight the personal journeys of faith. They emphasize that the challenges and triumphs of obedience are not unique to the Bishop but are shared by all believers, creating a sense of connection and solidarity among the viewers.
qAndA.question: How do the visual cuts to individuals in the church pews contribute to the video's overall message?

He flips the perspective, highlighting that everyone also has others who obey them.
He switches to English, emphasizing that humans are not simply followers or obeyers; they also have people who follow and obey them.
He observes that this obedience is not always based on direct orders but often stems from following good examples.
He emphasizes that above all, everyone obeys God.
He introduces the idea of different stages or chapters in obedience to God.
He mentions three stages of obedience.
He introduces the first stage, which he calls 'alay' (offering).

text_to_speech: Everyone must obey. All of us. Children obey their parents. Parents follow their boss in the workplace or those who are older than them. But we do not just follow. We also have those who follow us. We are not only people who obey. We are not only people who follow. We have also people who follow us. We have also people who obey us. Not as a result of giving commands but they follow by example. They follow by your good example. We all have that. And most of all, we all follow and obey God. But there are different kinds of followers. In different chapters. In different episodes. There are three chapters in discipleship. The first chapter of discipleship is what we could call ‘Alay’ (Offering/Sacrifice). Sacrifice – this means giving of oneself to the Lord. And in giving oneself to God, you are rewarded by that rewarding feeling knowing that you did the right thing. Sacrifice. An offering to the Lord. You will give an offering to God…an offering to the poor…an offering to those in need. And afterwards, you gain the best feeling in knowing that you did the right thing. But that is just elementary level. Did you ever notice that as you give more and more…with offering on top of another offering, we come to a point of exhaustion? There comes a point where you feel tempted and ask, Why do I keep on giving? There comes a point where you question– What am I doing here? What do I stand to gain from all this? And it’s not just that. You come to realize that with your offering comes a lot of hardships. I go to mass, I pray constantly…yet I am the one stricken with a sickness. But the one who never goes to mass, he is strong and healthy. I pray. I obey the commandments of God but why is this happening to me? Why did I become an orphan? Why am I the one being sued? Why am I the one suffering? Why are they talking behind my back? Why am I being punished? And you will start to queston – Lord, are you still there? Lord, do you still listen to my prayers…when I say – Lord, hear our prayers? What comes after Sacrifice? Aray (Pain). When you experience the pain and you’d say – Wait, please take it slow. Wait, this might break me. Wait, this might wound me. Wait, that hurts so much. Even so, the Lord never ceases in His call to follow Him. You are in pain. You are in pain because you want to do something but you are not able to. You are in pain because even if you’re doing the right thing, nothing good has come out of it. You are hurting because even if you want to offer the best to the Lord, your offering comes out uglier and uglier. And you wonder to yourself– Am I worthy to make an offering? When you come to a point that it is no longer beautiful…it is no longer sweet…it no longer beautiful music that plays in the background as we make our offering to the Lord but it is pain that we hear instead. Let us remind ourselves of the first sorrowful mystery. The agony in the garden. When the Lord said - Father, let this suffering pass me by. He was afraid. Father, why have you forsaken me? Aray (Ouch). I have long been suffering. Are you still there? But the call to serve remains. Follow me. And the third chapter, after Sacrifice and Pain, the Lord shall grant His mercy to be able to say – Amen. To be able to say unto the Lord – So what if I die? What if I get wounded? What if I bleed? What if I suffer? What if my burden becomes to heavy for me to bear? If all these came from you, Lord…Amen. Will I die in my old age? Will I die young? Will I be sent to prison because of you? Will be cursed, threatened because of you? When we come to a point in our lives when we must stand for our response to the Lord, I hope that we are able to say – Amen. And even in death, let us say unto the Lord – Lord, if I must die for your sake, I have but one prayer. May someone benefit from my death. Lord, if I am now called to die. I only ask you – Bless another person because of my death and my death will be meaningful and beautiful enough to be embraced. Three chapters. Alay. Aray. Amen. (Sacrifice. Pain. Amen.) If you are in that chapter of ‘Sacrifice’ and you are experiencing pain, you have the option to relax. You have the option of taking a vacation and stay in that chapter of ‘Sacrifice’. But if you are filled with courage, you will choose to endure the pain because in your heart, you know that…you are being molded by Jesus Christ. And when you find yourself in so much pain, and you feel so alone…look upon Him who is nailed to the cross and tell yourself this – Amen. It is finished. Into your hands I commend my spirit. And when we are eventually called to die and someone benefitted from our death…when we are laid to rest and something grew from our resting place, then we have really become disciples of the Lord. Today, my question to you is – Where are you as a follower/disciple? Honeymoon? Alay (Sacrifice)? That sweet feeling. Sense of lightness. Aray (Pain)? Dark. Heavy. Painful. Enduring the pain. Or Amen? Painful. Heavy. But no longer enduring because I am now content with the burden I carry, because in my heart, I know that He will never leave me behind. That is where God is. That is what discipleship means. Discipleship will not be easy. Discipleship will not be always convenient. Discipleship can be painful. But if you carry on, you’re going to become free of pain because your pain, united with Jesus, will set other lives free from sin. Where are you in your discipleship? Sacrifice….Pain…or Amen?

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Lahat ng tao ay ka ilang ang sumunod.
Magulang, sumosinun sa boss at rabao.
Tayurin ay merong sumosinun sa atin.
We are not only people who obey.
We are not only people who follow.
We have also people who follow us.
We have also people who obey us.
At hingit sa Lahat, tayo ng Lahat para parae hong sumosinod sa dios.
Pero ibaibaho ang uri ng Tagasunod.
Ang uunang yuktod ang pagsanod ay pede ko sa bihing alai.
Alai ibig sa bihing nagbibig ka ng sarili mo sa jos.
At pagkabigay mo ng sarili mo sa jos,
si nusokliyan ka naman ang jos na magandang pakiramdang na tamay ang gidawamo.
Alai, pagbibig ka sa dios, mag aalai ka sa dios ng buhay ng alai sa mahihirap,
ng alai sa mga nangang ang ilangan,
at pagkatapos na oon maganda yung pakiramdammu,
kasi alamong gumoha ka ng kabutihan.
Di bagyon na palsin sa ating buhay,
kapag bihay ka ng bihay, alai ka ng alai,
Domara ting din yung tukso na sa bihing,
Domara ting din yung tukso na,
ang dupa na kukuha ko dito,
na dupa ng napakal ako dito.
nag aalai ka ng nga pinahihirapan ka pa.
Nagsisimbakan naggada sel ka bakit ako mesakit.
Sa mantalah hindi na mga nagsisimba ay nat malakas.
Nagdada selako sa mosunod sa koma otos ng dios,
pero, bakit ako ang negaka ganitong,
panginod oon ang jangkaw ba ba?
Panginod ni kao pa ba yung sumosod
ka pagsina sabi kung panginod oon,
at para ang gusto mo sa bihin,
sa pagsisabi sa aking sumod ka sa aking.
meron kang gustoong gawin na hindi mo magawak.
mabuti yung ginaawamo ang soklisayo i-masama.
gusto mo magalay ng maganda sa dios,
pero papangit ng papangit yung inaalay mo
Kapan pagdumatig na yung yung yukto,
at aray na ang narinig natin.
Balika natin ang unang misterio ng habis,
Father, let this suffering pass me by,
bibi ang karin ng awan ng dios
ay ano ko mga matay ako?
Ayano ko mabigat yung daladal ako?
Kung galang sa inyo, panginod on?
Ikaw ko lumbako dahil sa inyo?
Mumurahin bako pagbaban takan ako dahil sa inyo?
Kapag doang mating yung yuktod ang ating buhay?
Panginod kung kailangan na pustalaga ako mo matay,
sana may makinabang sa aking kamataya.
if I am now called to die,
would be meaningful and beautiful enough to be embraced.
Pero kung matapang tapangan doon mo,
at kung saaling aray na alay kanata laga
tingnan mo lang yung nakapakos sa krus
At kung tayo ng aay mamatay
at may rung makinabang sa aking kamatayan,
at kung tayo ng aay ilibing
at may tububo sa aking libingan,
ang tanong kose ayo ay nasa ang ka
discipleship will not be always convenient.
you're going to be free from pain
because your pain united with Jesus
will set other lives free from sin.
